title: CYBER project reports suspicious bridge activity; Upbit and Bithumb suspend CYBER transfers
date_note: Liputan6 (published 22 November) says the project reported this on Saturday; 21 November 2026 was a Saturday.
place: South Korea (Upbit and Bithumb exchanges; the project's own location is not stated)
geo_basis: country of the two exchanges that halted transfers, as the source names them; the project's location is not given
summary: Liputan6, citing Cointelegraph, reports that the CYBER project said it detected unexpected minting of CYBER on Solana, followed by tokens moving out of the Ethereum lockbox on its cross-chain bridge. Upbit and Bithumb suspended CYBER deposits and withdrawals. The project says it is investigating which assets and bridge routes are affected and urged users not to use the bridge.
plain: A crypto project says it saw suspicious activity on its token bridge. Two South Korean exchanges paused deposits and withdrawals of its token while it investigates.
exec: A reported bridge problem at a token project led two South Korean exchanges to pause transfers; the project is still investigating.
action: As the project urges, do not use the CYBER bridge or deposit CYBER to exchanges while the investigation continues.

validation.note: Only Liputan6, relaying Cointelegraph, was read; the project's own statement and the exchanges' notices were not read. Cause and losses are not stated.
